4209.t: To the Paschal Victim let Christians offer their praises. The Lamb has redeemed the sheep: Christ, the sinless one, has reconciled sinners to the Father. Death and life have met in a wondrous combat: the Prince of life, who died, reigns living. Tell us, Mary, what didst thou see on the way? I saw the tomb of the living Christ, and the glory of the Risen One; the angelic witnesses, the napkin and the linen clothes. Christ my hope is risen: He goes before you into Galilee. We know that Christ is truly risen from the dead: do Thou, victorious King, have mercy on us. Amen. Alleluia.

4211.t: Praise, O Sion, thy Saviour, praise thy Leader and thy Shepherd in hymns and canticles. Dare as much as thou canst, for He is above all praise, nor canst thou praise Him enough. A special theme of praise, the living and life-giving Bread, is set before us today: the Bread which at the table of the holy Supper was truly given to the Twelve. Let our praise be full, let it ring out, let the joy of the soul be glad and seemly. For this is the solemn day on which the first institution of this table is recalled. At this table of the new King, the new Pasch of the new law ends the old Passover. The new puts the old to flight, the truth the shadow, light dispels the night. What Christ did at the Supper He commanded to be done in His memory. Taught by His holy ordinance, we consecrate the bread and wine as the Victim of salvation. This is the doctrine given to Christians: that bread is changed into His flesh and wine into His blood. What thou understandest not and seest not, a lively faith affirms beyond the order of nature. Under different species, signs only and not things, lie hidden wondrous realities. His flesh is food, His blood is drink; yet Christ remains whole under each species. By him who receives Him He is not cut, not broken, not divided: He is received whole. One receives, a thousand receive; as much as they, so much does he; nor once received is He consumed. The good receive Him, the wicked receive Him, but with unequal lot, of life or of destruction. Death to the wicked, life to the good: see how unlike the outcome of a like receiving. When the Sacrament is broken, doubt not, but remember that there is as much in each fragment as is hidden in the whole. There is no division of the substance, only a breaking of the sign, by which neither the state nor the stature of Him who is signified is lessened. Behold the Bread of Angels made the food of pilgrims: truly the bread of the children, not to be cast to dogs. It was foretold in figures when Isaac was offered, when the Paschal lamb was slain, when manna was given to the fathers. Good Shepherd, true Bread, Jesus, have mercy on us: feed us, protect us, make us see good things in the land of the living. Thou who knowest and canst do all things, who feedest us here as mortals, make us there Thy fellow guests, co-heirs and companions of the holy citizens of heaven. Amen. Alleluia.

4213.t: Come, Holy Spirit, and send forth from heaven the ray of Thy light. Come, Father of the poor; come, Giver of gifts; come, Light of hearts. Thou best of Comforters, sweet Guest of the soul, sweet refreshment. In labour Thou art rest, in heat the tempering, in weeping the solace. O most blessed Light, fill the inmost hearts of Thy faithful. Without Thy grace there is nothing in man, nothing that is harmless. Wash what is unclean, water what is dry, heal what is wounded. Bend what is rigid, warm what is cold, guide what has gone astray. Give to Thy faithful who trust in Thee the sevenfold gift. Give the reward of virtue, give the end of salvation, give everlasting joy. Amen. Alleluia.

4214.t: Let the choir of the faithful exult with joy. Alleluia. The womb of a spotless Virgin has brought forth the King of kings: a wondrous thing! The Angel of counsel is born of a Virgin, the Sun from a star: a Sun that knows no setting, a star ever shining, ever bright. As the star its ray, so the Virgin brings forth her Son in like manner. Neither the star by its ray, nor the Mother by her Son, is made less pure. The lofty cedar of Lebanon is likened to the hyssop in our valley; the Word, the Most High, deigned to become flesh, taking flesh. Isaias foretold it, the Synagogue remembers it, yet never does she cease to be blind. If not her own prophets, let her believe the Gentiles, in the Sibylline verses which foretold these things. Make haste, unhappy one, believe at least the ancient things: why wilt thou be condemned, wretched people? Behold the Child whom the Scripture announces: look upon Him whom His Mother bore. Alleluia.

4830.t: Alleluia. ℣. Grant, O Joseph, that we may pass our life in innocence, and may it ever be safe under thy patronage.

4850.t: The Holy Ghost will teach you, alleluia, whatsoever I shall have said to you, alleluia, alleluia.

4933.t: God hath established the world, which shall not be moved: thy throne, O God, is prepared from of old: thou art from everlasting.

4958.t: Alleluia. ℣. Come, O Lord, and do not delay: forgive the sins of Thy people Israel.

4988.t: Let them not eat of the holy things, till there arise a high priest learned and perfect.

4992.t: Alleluia. ℣. The white-robed army of Martyrs praiseth Thee, O Lord.

5072.t: Alleluia. ℣. Glorious father Vincent, illustrious son of the Order of Dominic, pour forth prayers to the supreme Judge for all the peoples devoted to thee.

5082.t: Moses consecrated an altar to the Lord, offering upon it holocausts and sacrificing victims: he made an evening sacrifice to the Lord God for an odour of sweetness, in the sight of the children of Israel.

5207.t: Alleluia. ℣. Blessed for his threefold fruit, whom his wondrous father, holy Dominic, chose for his manifold virtue.

5285.t: Praise ye the Lord, for he is good: sing ye to his name, for it is sweet: whatsoever he pleased, he hath done in heaven and in earth.

5286.t: Alleluia. ℣. I will save my people Israel in the evil day: and I will be their God, in truth and in justice.

5535.t: Alleluia. ℣. The Lord is risen from the sepulchre, who for us hung upon the tree.

5585.t: Praise be to Thee, O God. ℣. Herod in his wrath slew many children in Bethlehem of Juda, the city of David. Praise be to Thee, O God.

5767.t: Alleluia. ℣. The good Shepherd is risen, who laid down his life for his sheep, and vouchsafed to die for his flock.

5838.t: In the heavenly hierarchy let a new harmony resound with a new song; and let the melody of our choir on this pilgrim way accord with it, rejoicing with Dominic. Out of the Egypt of desolation the Maker of the world calls a man after His own will. In the basket of poverty he crosses the river of vanity for the salvation of the people. In the figure of a little dog the preacher to the world is shown beforehand to his mother: bearing a torch in its mouth, he exhorts the peoples to the rule of love. This is the new lawgiver, this the zealous Elias who detests every crime. He scatters the foxes of Samson, and with the trumpet of Gideon puts to flight the armies of the enemy. He restores to his mother her son called back from the dead, alive while he himself still lives in the body. At the sign of the cross the rain gives way; the company of the brethren eat the bread sent by God's gift. Happy is he, through whom the whole Church now, receiving joy, is exalted. He fills the world with seed; and at last he is placed among the hosts of heaven. The grain lay hidden, the star lay veiled in shadow; but the Maker of all things bids the bones of Joseph flourish and the star shine forth for the salvation of the nations. O how the fragrance of his tomb, surpassing every perfume, proves the flower of his flesh! The sick hasten and are healed; the blind and the lame are restored by many mighty works. Let us therefore sound the praises of wondrous Dominic with full voice. Let the needy people that follows in his footsteps cry out, seeking his help. But thou, father, loving and good, shepherd and patron of the flock, with prayer ever earnest, before the court of the supreme King commend for ever the cause of the flock thou hast left behind. Amen. Alleluia.

5877.t: The sorrowful Mother stood weeping beside the cross on which her Son was hanging. Through her soul, groaning, sorrowing and grieving, the sword had passed. O how sad and how afflicted was that blessed Mother of the Only-begotten! She mourned and grieved, the loving Mother, as she beheld the sufferings of her glorious Son. Who is the man who would not weep, seeing the Mother of Christ in such torment? Who could keep from sorrowing with her, beholding the Mother of Christ suffering with her Son? For the sins of His people she saw Jesus in torments and subjected to the scourges. She saw her sweet Son dying, forsaken, as He gave up His spirit. O Mother, fount of love, make me feel the force of thy sorrow, that I may mourn with thee. Make my heart burn with love of Christ my God, that I may please Him. Holy Mother, do this: fix the wounds of the Crucified deeply in my heart. Share with me the pains of thy wounded Son, who deigned to suffer so much for me. Let me weep with thee in loving devotion, and suffer with the Crucified as long as I live. To stand with thee beside the cross, and to join thee in thy lament, is my desire. Virgin of virgins most excellent, be not bitter to me now: let me weep with thee. Let me bear the death of Christ, make me a sharer in His passion, and keep His wounds in mind. Let me be wounded with His wounds, inebriated with the cross and the blood of thy Son. Lest I burn in the flames, let me be defended by thee, O Virgin, in the day of judgement. Christ, when I must go hence, grant that through Thy Mother I may come to the palm of victory. When my body dies, grant that my soul be given the glory of paradise. Amen. Alleluia.

5936.t: Hail, Queen of heaven, Mother of the King of Angels: O Mary, flower of virgins, like the rose or the lily: pour forth prayers to thy Son for the salvation of the faithful.

5947.t: This is my body, which shall be delivered for you: this chalice is the new testament in my blood, saith the Lord: this do ye, as often as you shall receive it, in commemoration of me.

6120.t: Blessed be the holy Trinity and undivided Unity: we will give glory to Him, because He hath shown His mercy to us. ℣. Let us bless the Father and the Son, with the Holy Ghost. Glory be to the Father.

6151.t: Thou gavest us bread from heaven, O Lord, having in it all that is delicious, and the sweetness of every taste.

6279.t: Be mindful, O Lord, of thy word which thou hast spoken: I desire not the death of the sinner, but that he be converted and live. And since it is not of him that willeth, but of thee that showest mercy: convert me to thee, and I shall be converted: save me, and I shall be saved, O Lord.

6300.t: He who deigned to heal me of every wound, and to restore my breast to my body, Him do I call upon, the living God.

6350.t: Alleluia. ℣. Christ is risen and hath shone upon his people, whom he redeemed with his blood.

6367.t: Absolve, O Lord, the souls of all the faithful departed from every bond of sin. ℣. And by the help of thy grace may they be found worthy to escape the judgement of vengeance, and to enjoy the bliss of everlasting light.

6422.t: Alleluia. ℣. Rejoice, my son Hyacinth, for thy prayers are heard by my Son: and whatsoever thou shalt ask, thou shalt obtain through my intercession.

6443.t: Alleluia. ℣. (The choir kneels as far as “Reple”, and sings the whole.) Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of thy faithful, and kindle in them the fire of thy love.

6454.t: I will not leave you orphans: I will come to you again, alleluia: and your heart shall rejoice, alleluia, alleluia.

6487.t: Andrew saith to his brother Simon: We have found the Messias, which is, being interpreted, the Christ. And he brought him to Jesus.

6589.t: He that shall meditate on the law of the Lord day and night, shall bring forth his fruit in due season.

6607.t: Behold the Lord will come, and all his saints with him: and there shall be in that day a great light.

6704.t: The day of wrath, that day shall dissolve the world in ashes, as David and the Sibyl bear witness. What trembling there shall be when the Judge shall come to examine all things strictly! The trumpet, scattering its wondrous sound through the tombs of every land, shall gather all before the throne. Death and nature shall be astonished when creation rises again to answer to the Judge. The written book shall be brought forth, in which all is contained whereby the world shall be judged. When the Judge is seated, whatever is hidden shall appear: nothing shall remain unpunished. What shall I, wretched one, say then? Whom shall I ask to plead for me, when even the just shall scarcely be safe? King of dreadful majesty, who freely savest those who are to be saved, save me, O fount of mercy. Remember, loving Jesus, that I am the cause of Thy journey: lose me not on that day. Seeking me, Thou didst sit down weary; Thou didst redeem me by suffering the cross: let not such labour be in vain. Just Judge of vengeance, grant the gift of pardon before the day of reckoning. I groan as one guilty; my face blushes for my sin: spare, O God, Thy suppliant. Thou who didst absolve Mary and didst hear the thief, hast given hope to me also. My prayers are not worthy, but Thou in Thy goodness deal kindly, lest I burn in everlasting fire. Give me a place among the sheep, and separate me from the goats, setting me on Thy right hand. When the accursed are confounded and given over to the bitter flames, call me with the blessed. I pray, kneeling and bowed down, my heart contrite as ashes: take Thou care of my end. Tearful will be that day on which guilty man shall rise from the ashes to be judged. Spare him then, O God. Loving Lord Jesus, give them rest. Amen.

6773.t: Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high: and behold the joy that cometh to thee from thy God.

6869.t: The high priest stood between the dead and the living, having a golden censer in his hand: and offering the sacrifice of incense, he appeased the wrath of God, and the plague ceased from the Lord.

6911.t: Alleluia. ℣. These are the two olive trees and the two candlesticks shining before the Lord: they have power to shut heaven with clouds, and to open its gates, for their tongues are become keys of heaven.

7164.t: Wicked men have risen up against me: without mercy they sought to kill me, and they spared not to spit in my face: with their lances they wounded me, and all my bones were shaken.

7200.t: The Lord Jesus, after He had supped with His disciples, washed their feet, and said to them: Know you what I have done to you, I your Lord and Master? I have given you an example, that as I have done to you, so you do also.

7208.t: Alleluia. ℣. Hail, Mother of mercy, Mother of hope and of grace, O Mary.

7542.t: There was a man in the land of Hus, whose name was Job, simple and upright, and fearing God: whom Satan besought that he might tempt him: and power was given him by the Lord over his possessions and his flesh: and he destroyed all his substance and his children: and he struck his flesh also with a grievous ulcer.

7550.t: Alleluia. ℣. The Nativity of the glorious Virgin Mary, sprung from the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Juda, of the noble line of David.
